beats.title: A downhill step goes wrong [00:00–00:10.5]
beats.text: This downhill step makes loss rise. We’re minimizing one bowl: half w squared. Start at w equals one; loss is point-five.

beats.title: The direction is right [00:10.5–00:21.4]
beats.text: At w equals one, slope is one. Gradient points uphill, right; its negative points left. Direction tells us where, not how far.

beats.title: The step is too long [00:21.4–00:31.7]
beats.text: The update subtracts learning rate times gradient. Set it to two-point-four: from one, we land at negative one-point-four, past the minimum.

beats.title: Check the destination [00:31.7–00:41.5]
beats.text: Crossing the bottom isn’t automatically bad. Here, loss rises from point-five to point-nine-eight. This step landed higher than it began.

beats.title: What controls overshoot? [00:41.5–00:50.5]
beats.text: Gradient gives the local slope; learning rate sets distance. In this curved bowl, two-point-four is too large for that slope.

beats.title: A shorter step [00:50.5–00:61.2]
beats.text: Keep the bowl and start; change rate to one-point-five. We still cross, but loss falls to point-one-two-five. Crossing alone isn’t failure.

beats.title: The takeaway [00:61.2–00:69.0]
beats.text: A step too large for the curve can raise loss. Real loss shapes change, so a safe learning rate can vary.
